address: 08 Nguyễn Giao, KP2, Quốc lộ 22, Củ Chi, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: The landmark bò tơ Củ Chi house — young free-range beef (calves only 5–6 months) served as a hotpot and grilled, wrapped in rice paper with dew-soaked bánh tráng and mountains of herbs. A 30-year Highway 22 institution reviewed by Việt Nam News as a southern classic worth the drive.
dish: bò tơ (young free-range beef, hotpot & grilled)

n: Bánh Canh Trảng Bàng Út Huệ
address: 88 Nguyễn Văn Rốp, Trảng Bàng, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
w: The Bùi-family bánh canh that defines Tây Ninh's most famous food stop — clear pork-bone broth, hand-cut chewy rice noodles and crisp boiled pork leg, eaten with a plate of fresh herbs. One of the two landmark bánh canh Trảng Bàng houses on Nguyễn Văn Rốp.
dish: bánh canh Trảng Bàng (pork-leg rice-noodle soup)

n: Bánh Canh Trảng Bàng Năm Dung
address: 90 Nguyễn Văn Rốp, Trảng Bàng, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
w: A bánh canh name Trảng Bàng locals have known since the 1950s, right beside Út Huệ — the same dew-soaked-rice-paper canon of clear broth, pork leg and hand-made noodles. The old-guard alternative for the town's signature bowl.
dish: bánh canh Trảng Bàng (pork-leg rice-noodle soup)

n: Bánh Tráng Phơi Sương Trảng Bàng
address: Trảng Bàng town, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
w: The town's other signature: dew-soaked rice paper, sun-dried by day then softened in the night dew, whose craft was named national intangible cultural heritage in 2016. Eaten as bánh tráng cuốn thịt luộc — soft-paper rolls of boiled pork belly, herbs and dipping salt. Buy fresh from Trảng Bàng makers or eat it rolled at any bánh canh house here.
dish: bánh tráng cuốn thịt luộc (dew-soaked rice-paper pork rolls)

n: Cơm Chay Long Hoa (Tây Ninh Vegetarian)
address: Long Hoa Market area, Hòa Thành, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
w: The densest vegetarian-food zone in Vietnam, feeding the Cao Đài faithful who fast at least 10 days a month — mì Quảng chay, bún riêu chay, vegetarian spring rolls and mock-meat skewers made from Tây Ninh soy and sesame. The Long Hoa cluster by the Holy See is the place to taste this deeply local chay tradition.
dish: cơm chay / bún riêu chay (Cao Đài vegetarian)

n: Bánh Tráng Muối Tôm Tây Ninh
address: Long Hoa Market, Hòa Thành, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
w: Tây Ninh's viral street snack and famous souvenir: rice-paper strips tossed with the province's signature muối tôm (shrimp-chili salt), dried shrimp, quail eggs, mango and herbs. The muối tôm — salt roasted with dried shrimp, garlic and chili — is the reason people bring bags of it home.
dish: bánh tráng trộn / muối tôm (chili-shrimp-salt rice-paper snack)

address: Trung An & Củ Chi town, Củ Chi, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: Củ Chi's beloved cassava — sweeter, chewier and more fragrant than elsewhere — steamed with pineapple leaf and eaten with sesame or chili salt, the same tuber that fed the tunnel fighters. A cheap, nostalgic roadside snack sold across the district.
dish: khoai mì hấp (steamed cassava with sesame salt)

address: Núi Bà Đen foothills, Tây Ninh, Vietnam
w: Mountain snails found only around Bà Đen, foraged after rain and cooked stuffed with grated coconut, steamed with lemongrass or ginger and dipped in salt-pepper-lime. A genuinely place-specific Tây Ninh delicacy eaten at the foot of the mountain.
